description: We are a team interested in new technology and innovating with different ideas in a way that has a benefit for tech development, This way we can provide many solutions for the storytelling of the moon discarded equipment.  We honor our name, Deep Striders, by taking steps across the lunar surface to clear the path for a sustainable space future and legacy.
summary:
We developed Deep Striders, an interactive lunar exploration and space archaeology 2D simulator playable directly in any web browser. Designed to be accessible and engaging for students, youth, and general audiences, the game puts players in control of the Strider-1 rover a specialized unit built to take "deep strides" into dark lunar craters and historic landing zones combining educational storytelling with realistic NASA engineering mechanics.

Deep Striders transforms NASA archives into an interactive storytelling game for youth , adressing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars" challenge. Players uncover the history of Apollo and Surveyor artifacts while applying NASA's heritage guidelines and the Artemis Accords. By scanning discarded hardware and deciding whether to preserve historical monuments or recycle operational debris via realistic ISRU mechanics, players learn space history and sustainable engineering.

With over 180 tons of past mission equipment on the Moon, future Moon explorers must learn to protect historic sites while recycling valuable materials for survival.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Players pilot the Strider-1 rover in a 2D lunar environment directly in their browser. Using telemetry radar , they locate discarded NASA hardware across sunlit plains and Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs).Players manage realistic constraints like solar battery recharge and extreme cold while reading each object's true story and choosing whether to preserve it as heritage or recycle its metals (ISRU) for a future lunar base.

 What benefits does it have? 

Designed for students, youth, and educators, the game requires no downloads and uses intuitive controls to make aerospace concepts easy to understand. By using STEM mechanics with historical storytelling, our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers to practice responsible space regulation protecting humanity’s cosmic heritage while building a sustainable circular economy on the Moon. And Getting the public to learn about the Artemis accords.

What is the intended impact of the project? 

To inspire the new generations to see space exploration not just as planting flags, but as responsible regulation protecting human milestones on the Moon and Mars while developing a sustainable, circular space economy, and emphasize the nonviolent space exploration .

Tools ,software and Data employed in the project

We developed the simulator on Rosebud AI (using HTML5 Canvas and JavaScript), which also generated the game's 2D visual assets and audio effects. Our narrative, lander operations, and heritage mechanics are grounded in official resources from NASA and SpaceX, including NASA's In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) , Artemis III mission and lander operations data, the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal , NASA’s Recommendations to Space-Faring Entities (Lunar Historic Sites), Section 9 of the Artemis Accords, and SpaceX’s Starship lunar mission specifications.

How is your project creative?

Instead of a passive slideshow or article, it turns NASA's technical heritage guidelines into an interactive moral and engineering dilemma embodying our team name, Deep Striders, by letting players literally "stride deep" into lunar craters as space archaeologists. This way we made a creative simulator rather than presenting space debris as a static catalog for schools and clear storytelling so players of all ages can immediately connect with the stories behind abandoned space equipment.

What factors did your team consider?

Realist mechanics and style of a game called "Moonbase Alpha" style with 2D gameplay that younger audiences can grasp in seconds, and simplify game mechanics ensuring players learn the history and why certain sites (like Apollo landing zones) are untouchable heritage, while spent rocket stages or thermal blankets can be safely recycled emphasizing the Artemis Accords .
